record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: What privacy-preserving debugging and interpretability methods can answer practical machine-learning workflow questions on decentralized user data, such as inspecting failure cases, outliers, or bias, and how can differentially private federated generative models be improved enough to support those uses faithfully?

evidence.quote: Developing privacy-preserving techniques to answer such questions on decentralized data is a major open problem. ... However, many open questions remain (see discussion in [31]), in particular the development of algorithms that improve the ﬁdelity of FL DP generative models.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let a population of $N$ clients each hold a private local dataset $D_i$ drawn from an unknown distribution $\mathcal{P}_i$ over a common data domain $\mathcal{X}$. A central server may interact with the clients only through a federated protocol: in each round it broadcasts a message, each participating client computes a local update from its own data, and the aggregated client messages are released to the server through a mechanism $\mathcal{M}$ that is $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differentially private at the user (client) level, i.e. for every pair of neighboring client populations differing in the data of a single user and every measurable event $S$,
$$\Pr[\mathcal{M}(\text{population}) \in S] \le e^{\varepsilon}\,\Pr[\mathcal{M}(\text{neighbor}) \in S] + \delta.$$
Raw examples in any $D_i$ may never be transmitted to the server or to a human analyst.

Practical workflow questions. A machine-learning practitioner training a model $f_\theta:\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y}$ on the federation needs to perform standard debugging and interpretability tasks on the union $\bigcup_i D_i$, including:
(a) inspecting representative failure cases on which $f_\theta$ errs;
(b) detecting and characterizing outliers or distribution shift between subpopulations of clients;
(c) auditing the model and the data for bias with respect to a sensitive attribute $A$;
(d) producing human-interpretable summaries or example-level explanations of model behavior.

Problem. 
1. Design a family of $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-user-level differentially private federated procedures $\{\mathcal{A}_q\}$, one for each workflow question $q$ in (a)–(d), that produce releases $\mathcal{A}_q(D_1,\dots,D_N)$ enabling the practitioner to faithfully answer $q$, and prove formal utility guarantees relating the answers obtained from $\mathcal{A}_q$ to the answers that would be obtained from direct inspection of $\bigcup_i D_i$.

2. Consider the special case where $\mathcal{A}_q$ is implemented by training a generative model $G_\phi$ over $\mathcal{X}$ via a federated, user-level $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-DP optimization procedure, and then answering workflow questions by drawing synthetic samples from $G_\phi$. Define a fidelity measure $\mathrm{Fid}(G_\phi,\mathcal{P})$ (for example, the total variation or Wasserstein distance to the underlying mixture $\mathcal{P} = \tfrac{1}{N}\sum_i \mathcal{P}_i$, or the gap between expectations of a chosen test class of statistics under $G_\phi$ and under $\mathcal{P}$). Develop training algorithms and theoretical analyses showing how $\mathrm{Fid}(G_\phi,\mathcal{P})$ can be made small enough — as a function of $\varepsilon$, $\delta$, $N$, the per-client sample size, the model class, and the data dimension — that synthetic samples from $G_\phi$ faithfully support the debugging and interpretability tasks (a)–(d), in the sense that decisions made by the practitioner from $G_\phi$-samples agree with decisions that would be made from the true data with high probability.

The goal is both to identify which workflow questions admit such privacy-preserving answers and to quantitatively improve the achievable fidelity of differentially private federated generative models to the level required by these uses.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., DP federated diffusion models for tabular data such as DP-Fed-FinDiff, federated synthetic data generation with DP, and explainable DP-FL frameworks like FedHDPrivacy) has produced partial advances on training higher-fidelity DP federated generative models and on using them as proxies for inspecting private decentralized data. However, the literature explicitly frames raising the fidelity of DP federated generative models to the level required for faithful debugging, outlier and bias inspection on decentralized user data as an active and unresolved research direction. No general solution with formal utility guarantees covering the full range of debugging and interpretability workflows is established.

status_evidence.title: Generative Models for Effective ML on Private, Decentralized Datasets
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes using DP federated generative models as auxiliary tools to debug data when raw inspection is forbidden, and notes that higher-fidelity models are needed for richer workflows.
status_evidence.claim: Frames DP federated generative models for debugging as a promising but only partially addressed direction.

status_evidence.title: Federated Diffusion Modeling with Differential Privacy for Tabular Data Synthesis (DP-Fed-FinDiff)
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces a DP federated diffusion framework aiming at high-fidelity synthetic tabular data and studies privacy/utility/fidelity trade-offs.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial progress on improving fidelity of DP federated generative models.

status_evidence.title: A Systematic Review of Federated Generative Models
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of federated generative modeling identifying open challenges including privacy, fidelity, and downstream usability.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms that fidelity of DP federated generative models remains an open research challenge.

status_evidence.title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning with Differentially Private Hyperdimensional Computing (FedHDPrivacy)
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes an explainable DP federated learning framework focusing on interpretability under DP guarantees.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on interpretability under DP-FL, not a full solution to private debugging workflows.
